title: Monads as pluggable function application via bind
why: Bind is function application with a hole for custom logic; Maybe shows how it composes computations cleanly.

title: Investor defends JustFab against scam accusations
why: Partisan defense by an investor citing engagement anecdotes; argument rather than substantive evidence about the business.

title: Speculative AI credit card pricing idea
why: Speculative business brainstorm about dynamic pricing through a credit card; no grounded technical or expert knowledge.

title: Why JavaScript's debugging tooling stands out
why: Monkey patching, live editing, time-travel debugging, and sourcemaps make JavaScript unusually inspectable and extensible.

title: Google Fi porting and support horror story
why: Personal complaint about a porting failure and customer support; a story without a transferable technical lesson.

title: Bitcoin malleability and the normalized txid fix
why: Transaction IDs can change before confirmation; exchanges adopting a normalized hash index can track withdrawals reliably.

title: Personal story about surname and identity
why: Personal narrative about a surname and transition; no technical or transferable lesson for a general reader.

title: Personal account of testing and school misery
why: Personal anecdote about childhood testing and schooling; reflective but not an informational lesson.

title: European perspective on America's decline
why: Opinion and generalization about American society and culture; no substantive evidence or technical insight.

title: How fair use's four factors applied to Google Books
why: Shows fair use turns on four statutory factors, and why whole-work copying for public benefit can still qualify.

title: Why hiring defined impact as shipped code
why: Interviewers equated getting things done with writing shipped code, leaving designers and other non-coding impact unmeasured.

title: Reframing unit tests as executable documentation
why: Treat any interface as a unit and tests as documenting what it does, rather than proving correctness in isolation.

title: Author's preferred language for web apps
why: Personal preference for Perl over Haskell and Common Lisp, driven by library availability; mostly opinion.

title: Concerns over SpaceX and Boca Chica residents
why: Political and environmental argument about eminent domain and wildlife; not a technical explanation.

title: Why canvas-based GUIs hurt accessibility and integration
why: Canvas and WebGL widgets bypass the DOM accessibility layer and lose native scrolling, clipboard, and zoom behavior.

title: What EU Article 11 actually permits and excludes
why: Quoted text exempts private non-commercial use and mere hyperlinks with individual words, which many news summaries omit.

title: Argument for starting a company solo
why: Argument about cofounders built on analogies to divorce statistics; persuasion rather than substantive insight.

title: Why RubyGems resists fleet-wide system administration
why: Gems bypass OS package managers, and installs needing interactive prompts defeat scripted deployment across many servers.

title: Why lock files still matter despite functional package managers
why: Pure hashed builds are powerful, but application developers still need resolution and easy config swapping, not full-graph specs.

title: Where expert-level science and foreign policy analysis lives
why: Primary sources like IPCC summaries and think-tank publications beat popular coverage, which often gets the questions wrong.

title: Most famous inventors came from modest backgrounds
why: Examples like George Green and Benjamin Franklin show innovators were mostly middle or working class, not aristocratic dilettantes.

title: Why CMS backends should expose APIs, not pages
why: A content tool should only serve an API; rendering and page composition belong to separate components, improving security and decoupling.

title: Why resident work-hour limits didn't change mortality
why: Restrictions cut resident car accidents but left complications and mortality unchanged, plausibly because attendings deliver much care.

title: Why HP's printer business is really an ink business
why: Refill ink is cheaper to sell than cartridges, so ink revenue shapes HP's printer and cartridge strategy in ways outsiders miss.

title: Argument about selling ideas to large companies
why: Opinion on intrapreneurship and corporate decision makers; persuasive commentary without concrete evidence.

title: Four practical lessons on data, sales, and rollout
why: Use measurements over guesses, find the real objection beyond price, and launch systems early so users fix the data.

title: How to start learning math through logic and proofs
why: Math has many branches sharing ground; learn proof language first, where programming helps, then study one branch intensely.

title: SSA is functional by accident, not by design
why: SSA was invented to speed dataflow analysis; its resemblance to functional programming was a side observation, not the goal.

title: Complaint about moving software into browsers
why: Opinion lamenting web-based software and JavaScript; a cultural rant without technical substance.

title: Why toy models reproducing relativity prove little
why: Models can match relativity or quantum behavior in limits while missing most physics; generic systems aren't theories by default.

title: Personal experience moving from US to Europe
why: Personal life report and opinion about quality of life; no technical or transferable informational lesson.

title: Treat hiring as a tracked funnel with mission
why: Track hiring funnel data from the start, write candidate-focused job descriptions, and measure how screens predict later success.

title: Many mocks signal code that needs restructuring
why: A unit test needing many mocks usually means the function should be split; restructure the code rather than the test strategy.

title: Anecdotes about prime prize claimants
why: Entertaining stories about persistent crank claimants; no technical lesson beyond the fact that claimants persist.

title: Praise for an article about Walter Pitts
why: Appreciation of a linked article with little original information or explanation in the comment itself.

title: Why mandatory boilerplate comments degrade code
why: Required doc comments on self-explanatory methods add noise; comments should explain what the code cannot say.

title: Gendered expectations of confidence at work
why: Social commentary on gender and workplace perception; opinion-based and not a technical insight.

title: Personal account of police encounter after breakdown
why: Personal narrative about a mental health crisis and police contact; no transferable informational lesson.

title: Critique of Orwell's essay on language
why: Rhetorical critique with weak evidence and self-described incoherence; mostly argument rather than instruction.

title: Why phone photos fail beyond small screens
why: Phone photos look fine on small screens but degrade in prints and large monitors, per a professional photographer's experience.

title: Reflections on PHP and language popularity
why: Personal reflection on language popularity and career choice; opinion without a transferable technical lesson.

title: Correct framing of random variables and distributions
why: A random variable is a quantity measured across repeated experiments; its distribution is given by probabilities like P(X <= x).

title: Critique of FSF's Respects Your Freedom certification
why: Argument that RYF certification harms hardware freedom; opinion and advocacy rather than explanation.

title: Advice on overcoming loneliness via a partner
why: Personal life advice centered on a significant other; opinion-based, not an informational technical resource.

title: Reply disputing tone and moral framework
why: Argumentative exchange about tone and emotion versus rationality; no informational content on its own.

title: Django restricts template logic; Rails allows it
why: Django constrains template logic to enforce separation, while Rails permits Ruby in views but still separates app logic; PHP's mess isn't inherent.

title: Personal diet rules after weight gain
why: Personal anecdote about cutting bread and snacks; useful to the author, but mainly individual experience.

title: Why GNU HURD chose a microkernel design
why: Insider account: the microkernel aimed to give users control over daemons, at the cost of performance from extra context switches.

title: Erlang's strengths and why newcomers struggle
why: Simple syntax and built-in concurrency are strong points, but weak tooling and beginner onboarding hinder adoption.

title: Identity-aware proxies to avoid repeated logins
why: A proxy can sign identity tokens so apps need no login logic; securing bring-your-own devices is the hard part.

title: Recursion's essence is self-reference, not iteration
why: Recursion differs from loops because a definition uses itself; teach that element directly instead of calling recursion hard.

title: A tiny tool pulled in a huge dependency tree
why: glslify, meant as a simple file loader, installed a deep npm dependency tree, illustrating the hidden cost of dependencies.

title: Controlled studies challenge static typing claims
why: Controlled experiments like Hanenberg's show static typing's benefits are unproven; commonsense claims about fewer runtime errors need testing.

title: User impressions of Surface Pro hardware
why: Personal product impressions and speculation about Haswell timing; subjective, without broadly useful technical insight.

title: Reading of a criminal complaint's ambiguity
why: Commentary on a specific criminal case and its evidence; contextual and argumentative rather than a general lesson.

title: Chinese national's defense of government policy

title: Factual context on Oberlin bakery incident
why: News-event narrative and politics about a campus protest; contextual, not a broadly informative technical or expert lesson.

title: Rambling about disagreement and certainty

title: Argument on federal regulation and speech
why: Constitutional argument about regulatory power and militia wording; contested legal opinion, not an informational explanation.

title: Why US metros struggle: parking, sprawl, and density

title: Nostalgia for fast legacy software
why: Opinion praising legacy software speed and criticizing web bloat; anecdotal rather than instructive.

title: Get more from college by seeking challenge

title: Personal account of a poor Google interview
why: Personal complaint about one virtual interview; anecdote without a generalizable lesson about hiring.

title: Writer's introduction to craft and style

title: Speculation on Ukraine war and sanctions
why: Geopolitical speculation about war economics and sanctions; opinion and forecasting rather than verified expertise.

title: Three reasons copyright is hard to get right

title: Fear of drone surveillance and targeting
why: Emotional policy opinion about police helicopters and drones; no informational content.

title: Personal career dilemma in Brazil
why: Personal request for advice about job security and meaning; situational, not a generalizable informational lesson.

title: Lease clauses aren't automatically enforceable

title: How flexible office space business models work
why: Landlords use long leases to service debt; flexible-space operators take risk on vacancy and charge more to compensate.

title: Personal experience switching between Mac and Windows
